spans.note: leading blank line and package imports
blank lines and RNG seed fixed to 42

spans.operation: load the full soccer dataset from a fixed file path as the analysis source
average the two raters' ratings into a single continuous skin-tone score
bucket the continuous skin-tone score into light/dark categories using 0.25 and 0.75 cutoffs, leaving the middle range unlabeled
collapse red card counts into a binary outcome for having received any red card
drop players whose skin tone fell in the unlabeled middle band, restricting analysis to clearly light or dark cases
encode the treatment indicator so that dark skin tone is coded 1 and light is the reference 0

collapse the many free-text playing positions into a small set of coarse position groups (Forward/Winger, Midfielder, Defender, Goalkeeper, Other, Unknown) via keyword matching, then apply this mapping to every player
log-transform games played to use as a covariate instead of the raw count
narrow the working data down to just the outcome, treatment, covariates, and identifiers that will enter the model
one-hot encode position group and league country, dropping the first level of each as the reference category

spans.note: '# Set up X and y' comment
pulls out the already-defined outcome column
mechanically collects the dummy column names created by the earlier encoding step

spans.operation: choose the covariate/adjustment set for the regression (treatment, log games, position dummies, league dummies) and add an intercept term
choose to cluster standard errors by player rather than treat observations as independent
fit a logistic regression for the binary red-card outcome with cluster-robust standard errors and suppressed convergence output
compute average marginal effects (dy/dx at overall means) rather than reporting raw logit coefficients

spans.note: extracts the summary frame and the darkSkin row from the margeff object; trailing blank line

spans.operation: designate the marginal-effect risk difference for darkSkin (with its CI and p-value) as the primary estimand to report

spans.note: pulls the raw darkSkin coefficient and its standard error out of the fitted model

spans.operation: back out an adjusted odds ratio as a secondary estimand and build its confidence interval via a normal (1.96 SE) approximation on the log-odds scale

spans.note: prints the primary risk-difference estimand, CI, and p-value
prints the secondary odds-ratio estimand and CI
